title: Tiered declassification retention orchestrator and automated attestation for inference artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and deliver a retention orchestration feature that applies context-aware, tiered retention policies to inference artifacts (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics) and produces cryptographically-signed attestation bundles for compliance evidence. The system should support declassification rules (automatically change retention tiers after redaction or low-sensitivity classification), per-tenant overrides, legal-hold exceptions, and a preview/simulation UI for upcoming purges.

Motivation:
- Customers need deterministic, auditable deletion and export controls across multiple artifact classes: prompts/responses, request logs, and derived metrics.
- Current retention work focuses on static TTLs; we need dynamic, content-aware transitions (e.g., PII redaction => move to shorter retention, system prompts => longer archived retention).
- Compliance teams require signed artifacts that prove what was stored and when it was deleted/exported.

Goals:
1) Allow operators to declare multi-stage retention lifecycles with declassification transitions (e.g., raw -> redacted -> aggregated -> archive/purge).
2) Provide automatic classification hooks and redaction integration to trigger declassification transitions.
3) Generate time-stamped, KMS-signed evidence bundles for any retention action (archive, export, purge) including manifest and hashes.
4) Expose a simulator and preview UI in the Console to show future purges and allow legal-hold exceptions.
5) Surface per-route, per-model and per-tenant override rules with deterministic precedence and audit trails.

Proposal / High-level design:
- Retention lifecycle: define named stages (ephemeral, short-term, medium-term, long-term, archived, purged). Each stage has rules: duration, storage class, encryption key, residency region(s), and output behavior (retain, agg-only, delete).
- Declassification transitions: rules that move artifacts between stages based on signals: automated PII score, manual redaction API, system-level classification (model/system prompts), or time-based promotion.
- Evidence attestation: when a transition occurs (especially archive or purge), produce a signed bundle containing: artifact IDs, manifests (SHA256 per artifact), timestamps, origin route and model, tenant ID, and operation reason. Bundles are signed with customer or Redwood KMS keys and stored in a tamper-evident bucket.
- Simulation and preview: Console page that accepts active retention rules and produces a time-series preview of upcoming deletions/archives for a selected tenant, route, and date range. Support "what-if" adjustments without applying changes.
- APIs and CLI: REST endpoints to (a) upsert retention lifecycles, (b) submit manual declassification/redaction, (c) place/remove legal holds, (d) request signed evidence bundles on-demand. A lightweight CLI will allow export and attestation retrieval for auditors.

Data model (simplified):
- retention_policy: id, name, stages[]
- stage: name, duration_days, storage_class, residency_regions[], kms_key_alias, aggregation_allowed (true/false)
- transition_rule: trigger_type (pii_score_threshold/manual/redaction/system-tag/time), parameters
- artifact_record: id, tenant_id, route, model, current_stage, created_at, last_modified, sensitivity_score, legal_hold (bool)

UX/Console features:
- Policy editor: visual builder for stages and transitions (drag/drop stages, attach triggers).
- Preview simulator: timeline and counts, exportable CSV and PDF for auditors.
- Evidence center: search for attestation bundles by artifact id, tenant, date, operation type. Downloadable signed bundles and verification helper.
- Legal hold management: tenant-level UI to apply and comment on holds, with expiration or manual release.

Acceptance criteria:
- PM/Design: interactive policy editor mockups reviewed and signed off by Compliance/Legal.
- Engineering: APIs to create/modify policies and submit declassification/redaction calls; background worker that moves artifacts across stages; attestation bundle generator that signs with test KMS key.
- QA: end-to-end test that simulates PII scoring -> transition -> attach legal hold -> release -> purge prevented while hold active -> evidence bundle for purge once hold released.
- Security: KMS integration and signing flow reviewed by Security and documented; signing keys never exported in plaintext.
- Observability: metrics for number of transitions, time-to-transition, evidence bundle generation latency, and failed signings.

Success metrics:
- Reduce manual evidence request SLA from 72 hours to <= 6 hours for 90% of requests (measured during pilot).
- 95% accuracy in staged transitions for synthetic PII-labeled test set (evaluation harness).
- Simulator adoption: 30% of pilot tenants using preview UI before policy changes.

Rollout plan:
1) Design sprint (2 weeks): complete mocks, edge cases and API contract.
2) API + backend prototype (4 weeks): retention policy CRUD, background worker, simple in-memory attestation generator.
3) Pilot with 3 customers (6 weeks): enable per-tenant policies, feedback loop.
4) KMS signing + S3/Tiered archive integration (3 weeks) and security review.
5) Console polish and CLI (2 weeks).
6) General availability with migration guide (2 weeks).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect deletion due to misconfigured transitions. Mitigation: default to conservative behavior (never auto-purge without explicit confirmation), provide dry-run/simulator and two-step policy apply with staged activation.
- Risk: attestation signing keys compromise legal value. Mitigation: use KMS/HSM and rotate keys, provide customer-managed key option for enterprise.
- Risk: performance impact when scanning large volumes for transitions. Mitigation: incremental background workers, index artifacts by stage and next_transition_at, and batch attestation generation.

Dependencies and links:
- Depends on: ENG-22456 (deterministic purge orchestrator), PM-73145 (retention sculptor and evidence assembly).
- Links: design board (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/retention/tiered-declassification (placeholder), audit spec draft: drive.google.com/example-audit-spec (placeholder), infra RFC: github.com/redwood/rfcs/policies/retention-orch (placeholder).

Notes / open questions:
- Should attestation bundles include redacted artifact payloads or only hashes and metadata? We prefer hashes by default and include redacted snapshots when tenant consents.
- How to handle cross-region residency when artifact transitions to archived tier? Need a policy resolver that enforces residency constraints at transition time.
- Estimate may change after design sprint; initial estimate is 8 points.

Deliverables:
- API spec and OpenAPI file for retention lifecycle endpoints.
- Console policy editor and simulator screens.
- Background transition worker implementation and integration tests.
- KMS-backed evidence signing and download endpoints.
- Migration playbook for customers with existing TTLs.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Policy editor mocks approved by Compliance and Design.
2) Backend can apply policies and perform stage transitions for a subset of artifacts.
3) Evidence bundles produced on transitions and verifiable via KMS signature.
4) Simulator correctly shows future purges for provided date ranges.
5) Legal hold prevents purge actions until explicitly released.
notes: This ticket focuses on the orchestration and attestation pieces rather than deep ML PII detection accuracy. PII scoring integration will be a collaborative contract with Applied ML. Consider a follow-up ticket for auto-redaction pipelines that store redacted payloads alongside original hashes.
